summary: Client book length mismatch resulting in crash
description: Editing (already once edited) books with colored content makes the client mismatch the actual character length, resulting in either one character too much (takes away another character) or too less ( or following character still left) being deleted when removing characters. Concrete steps to reproduce: - start a 1.13.2 client, create a new singleplayer world, copy and paste any text with characters in a book (see below), save world - start a 1.14.x client, convert open the world, open the book Or use the following command in 1.14.x: setblock oak_sign{Text1:"{ "text ": "Click me ", "clickEvent ":{ "action ": "run_command ", "value ": " give p writable_book{pages:[ " u00a7nVery cool text n u00a7r u00a7 u00a7 u00a7 u00a7 hi n u00a75more n u00a7etext "]} "}}"} What can be observed: - clicking on or marking the last character of the book - crash - going to the last character with the right arrow doesn t go to the very end, but stops at a character before it - trying to remove characters where a is results in seemingly the wrong character being removed - most notably: clicking the front on the second last line, then pressing the delete backspace key removes characters a few letters behind the actually selected position This means that on a click in lines containing the position character length is calculated wrongly i.e. copy and paste nVery cool text r hi 5and even more etext The older 1.14.3 crash log had a different stacktrace , this is the latest 1.15.2: crash-2020-04-28_15.38.46-client.txtjava.lang.StringIndexOutOfBoundsException: String index out of range: 44 at java.base java.lang.StringLatin1.charAt(StringLatin1.java:48) at java.base java.lang.String.charAt(String.java:711) at dch.a(SourceFile:454) at dha.mouseClicked(SourceFile:779) at dbo.b(SourceFile:86) at dgb.wrapScreenError(SourceFile:447) at dbo.a(SourceFile:86) at dbo.c(SourceFile:150) at ais.execute(SourceFile:94) at dbo.b(SourceFile:150) at org.lwjgl.glfw.GLFWMouseButtonCallbackI.callback(GLFWMouseButtonCallbackI.java:36) at org.lwjgl.system.JNI.invokeV(Native Method) at org.lwjgl.glfw.GLFW.glfwPollEvents(GLFW.java:3101) at com.mojang.blaze3d.systems.RenderSystem.flipFrame(SourceFile:98) at cxx.e(SourceFile:301) at dbn.d(SourceFile:1012) at dbn.d(SourceFile:619) at net.minecraft.client.main.Main.main(SourceFile:204)
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Start a Minecraft client running version 1.13.2.
2. Create a new singleplayer world in Creative mode with default settings.
3. Obtain a book and quill by using the command `/give @p book_and_quill`.
4. Open the book and quill and paste the following text: `u00a7nVery cool text n u00a7r u00a7 u00a7 u00a7 u00a7 hi n u00a75more n u00a7etext`.
5. Save and exit the book.
6. Exit the game.
7. Start a Minecraft client running version 1.14.x.
8. Load the previously created world to convert it.
9. Open the saved book from your inventory.
10. Attempt to edit the text by clicking on or marking the last character of the book and observe the behavior, such as crashes, incorrect character deletion, or unexpected cursor positioning.
Environment: Minecraft Java Edition Versions: 1.14, 1.14.1 Pre-Release 1, 1.14.1 Pre-Release 2, 1.14.1, 1.14.2 Pre-Release 1, 1.14.2 Pre-Release 2, 1.14.2 Pre-Release 3, 1.14.2 Pre-Release 4, 1.14.2, 1.14.3 Pre-Release 1, 1.14.3 Pre-Release 2, 1.14.3 Pre-Release 3, 1.14.3, 1.14.4 Pre-Release 5, 1.14.4 Pre-Release 6, 1.14.4 Pre-Release 7, 1.14.4, 1.15.1, 1.15.2, 20w17a (includes snapshots)
Observed Behavior:
The client book length mismatch resulting in crashes occurs when editing books that have already been edited and contain colored content. This issue causes the client to incorrectly calculate the actual character length, leading to either one character too much or too little being deleted when removing characters. To reproduce this bug, start with a 1.13.2 client, create a new singleplayer world, copy and paste text with formatting into a book, save the world, then open it in a 1.14.x client to observe the issue. Alternatively, use the command `setblock oak_sign{Text1:"{ "text ": "Click me ", "clickEvent ":{ "action ": "run_command ", "value ": " give p writable_book{pages:[ " u00a7nVery cool text n u00a7r u00a7 u00a7 u00a7 u00a7 hi n u00a75more n u00a7etext "]} "}}"} in a 1.14.x client.

When interacting with the book, clicking or marking the last character results in a crash. Attempting to navigate to the last character using the right arrow key stops one character before the end. Deleting characters where a formatting code is present leads to incorrect removals; for instance, pressing delete on the second-to-last line removes characters several positions behind the selected position. This indicates that the client incorrectly calculates character length in lines with specific formatting codes.

The issue manifests as a `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` when the calculated index goes out of range, causing the game to crash. The latest 1.15.2 crash log provides detailed information on this exception: `java.lang.StringIndexOutOfBoundsException: String index out of range: 44`. This bug highlights a critical flaw in how the client handles formatted text within books across different versions, leading to unexpected behavior and crashes when editing such content.
Expected Behavior: When editing a book with colored content in a converted world, the client should accurately match the actual character length. Characters should be deleted correctly without causing crashes or mismatches. The cursor should move to the very end of the text when using the right arrow key, and deleting characters should remove the correct ones based on the selected position.
